newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Macfarlane says RBA independent for a decade.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Macfarlane says RBA independent for a decade.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) has only recently been seen as a reasonably independent central bank, despite the fact it has always had a high degree of legislative independence, Governor Ian Macfarlane said.

Macfarlane, in his first speech as governor since taking up his appointment last week, said there were a number of reasons for this perception, but he believed the bank had been largely independent from the second half of the 1980s.

The Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy issued on August 14, when Macfarlane's appointment was announced, "was a means of clearing up any ambiguity about the relationship between the Government and the Reserve Bank," he said.

"Although we are now getting recognised as a reasonably independent central bank, this is only a very recent phenomenon," Macfarlane told an economists' conference, adding that his predecessor, Bernie Fraser, had to constantly defend the RBA against charges of politicial interference.
"In my view, it (the RBA) has been clearly independent in the 1990s, and a good case can be made to show that it was largely independent in the second half of the 1980's," he said.

Perceptions of a lack of independence dated from before deregulation of financial markets which started in the early 1980's, when while the bank had legislative independence, it "did not have the instruments of monetary policy at its disposal -- before deregulation, they were nearly all in Canberra."
"Major decisions on monetary policy were made by the Monetary Policy Committee of Cabinet," he said.
Before deregulation, the Treasurer also determined interest rates, and M3 target, and the exchange rate was decided by a committee of three or four, including the RBA Governor.

"The big change for the Reserve Bank was deregulation," he said, as it swept away interest rate controls, freed up the exchange rate and made it possible to finance the budget deficit fully at market determnined rates.
Open market operations, which effectively determined short term monetary policy rates, was left as the only instrument of monetary policy, he said.
"This was entirely in the hands of the Reserve Bank, which put us operationally in the same position as the U.S. Federal Reserve or the Bundesbank," Macfarlane said.
Macfarlane said the recent statement on monetary policy was a continuation of the direction under the previous government, and showed the essentially bipartisan approach that now exists.
While the statement had increased perceptions of the RBA's independence, it should also be seen as part of a more general trend towards establishing a framework for better economic policy, he said.

"The statement was well received in Australia, and we have received feedback that it was well received overseas, including by a couple of overseas central banks which showed considerable interest in it," Macfarlane said.
